result.topic_en: Latin draft text for the Paris prize essay on heat conduction, summarizing the cases (m = 1, 2, 3, 4) in which the temperature in a homogeneous body can be a function of time and of only two variables, for the equation $\sum \partial^2 u/\partial x_i^2 = a\,\partial u/\partial t$.
result.transcription:
tuendae, quo pacto omnes casus inveniantur, in quibus temperatura $u$ [-functio temporis et duar-] in corporibus homogeneis functio temporis et duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit.
Sed angustia temporis non permisit, hos calculos perscribere. Contenti igitur esse debemus [-solutiones singulas quaestionis propositae-] postquam methodos, quibus usi sumus, {+[?]+} exposuimus, solutiones singulas quaestionis propositae enumerasse.
[-Sed-] [-Brevitatis-] Brevitatis causa casum simplicissimum, quando $u$ {+temperatura+} secundum legem
$I \quad \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_3^2} = a a \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
variatur, solum respiciemus, ad quem casus reliquos facile reduci posse constat;
Casus $m=1$ [-evenire-] [-tum-] tantum evenire potest, quando {+aut+} [-aut-] $u$ est constans {+aut in lineis rectis parallelis, aut in circulis+} [-in-] {+aut+} helicibus {+[?]+} [-ata-] ut coordinatis
{+rectangularibus+} [-simplicioribus-] $x, $ {+radii+} $r$ {+[?]+} rite [-in-] electis {+poni+} [-possit-] $\alpha = r$, $\beta = $ [-$\frac{\ldots}{x + \ldots}$-] $z + \epsilon\,\mathrm{const.}$, [-denotantibus a & b-] [-aut in circulis-]
Casus $m=2$ locum invenit, si $u = f(\alpha) + \varphi(\beta)$, Casus $m=3$, si $u = \alpha e^{\lambda t} + f(\beta)$ denotante $\lambda$ [-realem-] constantem
realem, casus denique $m=4$, ut {+jam+} supra invenimus, si $u$ est aut $= \alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + \mathrm{const}$, aut $= (\alpha$ [-$t$-] $+ \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + \mathrm{const}$
aut $= f(\alpha)$.
[-Tamen-] {+Quo+} Ut formae {+functionis $\alpha$+} [-functionis u penitus-] penitus innotescant, [-quod tantum est-] [-observare-] {+annotare+} tantum opus est,
[-u tum-] {+temperaturam+} [-functionem-] $u$, nisi sit formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, tum tantum functionem {+temporis et+} unius variabilis esse posse, quando
sit constans aut in planis parallelis, aut in sphaeris concentricis aut in cylindris eadem axi gaudentibus
[-Praeterea observamus in casu quarto $\lambda$ & $\mu$ constantes complexas conjugatas-]
Si $u$ est formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, [-ex aequatione-] differentiali I requiritur
$\frac{\partial^2 \alpha}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 \alpha}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 \alpha}{\partial x_3^2} = \lambda a a \alpha$
et perinde in casu quarto [-functiones-], substituendo valores ipsius $u$ in aequatione differentiali (I), functiones $\alpha$ & $\beta$ facile determinantur, dummodo [-obs-] animadvertatur, in hoc casu $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$ & $\beta e^{\mu t}$ [-const-] {+posse+} esse quantitates complexas conjugatas.

methods.what: Heat equation in three dimensions taken as the basic case
methods.quote: $I \quad \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x_3^2} = a a \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$

methods.what: Case m=1: u constant, or constant on parallel lines, circles or helices, with suitably chosen coordinates
Case m=2: temperature as a sum of functions of the two variables
Case m=3 form of the solution
methods.quote:
Casus $m=3$, si $u = \alpha e^{\lambda t} + f(\beta)$ denotante $\lambda$ [-realem-] constantem
realem

methods.what: Case m=4 forms of the solution
methods.quote:
si $u$ est aut $= \alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + \mathrm{const}$, aut $= (\alpha$ [-$t$-] $+ \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + \mathrm{const}$
aut $= f(\alpha)$

methods.what: Separated form u = α e^{λt} reduces the heat equation to a Helmholtz-type equation for α

items.quote: ad quem casus reliquos facile reduci posse constat
items.english: to which it is known that the remaining cases can easily be reduced

items.quote:
$u$, nisi sit formae $\alpha e^{\lambda t}$, tum tantum functionem {+temporis et+} unius variabilis esse posse, quando
sit constans aut in planis parallelis, aut in sphaeris concentricis aut in cylindris eadem axi gaudentibus
items.english: u, unless it is of the form α e^{λt}, can be a function of time and one variable only when it is constant either on parallel planes, or on concentric spheres, or on cylinders having the same axis

items.quote: Sed angustia temporis non permisit, hos calculos perscribere.
items.english: But lack of time did not permit writing out these calculations.

items.quote: in casu quarto [-functiones-], substituendo valores ipsius $u$ in aequatione differentiali (I), functiones $\alpha$ & $\beta$ facile determinantur
items.english: in the fourth case, by substituting the values of u into differential equation (I), the functions α and β are easily determined
